summary: Feed s130_double is degraded: 11.9% TCP packet drops (186/1557 packets) correlated with 1.42 Gbps microbursts exceeding the 1 Gbps SIEM port (142% capacity, 5 intervals). Overload is causing buffer tail-drops and incomplete SIEM ingestion.

findings.root_cause: Microburst buffer overflow: 1.42 Gbps peaks exceed the 1 Gbps SIEM ingress and packet broker buffers, causing tail drops. 186 of 1557 TCP packets (11.9%) show missing data/gaps, directly correlated with overloaded 1ms intervals.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM receives incomplete TCP flows and events; reassembly and correlation fail, creating forensic gaps, missed detections and false negatives for coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute s130_double across 2x1G SIEM inputs or broker load-balance group to absorb 1.42 Gbps bursts below 1 Gbps per port and eliminate buffer drops. Safe for this SIEM as needs_both_directions=false, no flow affinity required.

findings.root_cause: Feed aggregation delivers 1.42 Gbps peak in 1ms burst vs 1 Gbps SIEM port capacity (142% of line rate, 5 overloaded intervals). Single 1G tool port is undersized for the burst profile.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM NIC discards excess traffic during bursts before ingestion; events lost, ingestion queues overflow, alerts delayed or missing, reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: SIEM has needs_full_payload=false, so truncating payload after ~512 bytes preserves headers/metadata for detection while cutting burst bandwidth well below 1 Gbps. Alternatively add load-balance port if full payload retention required.
